# Generated markdown

The `.dd.md` sibling is the human view of a `.dd.json` source. The exemplar plan
begins:

```markdown
<!-- GENERATED by `node_modules/.bin/dd build` — do not hand-edit; regenerate from the .dd.json. -->
# Deterministic documents (dd)

**Schema**: builder/plan · **Source**: plan.dd.json · **Sections**: 5

<a id="meta"></a>

## Meta
```

The banner, heading, metadata, anchors, section bodies, and final newline are
part of the canonical bytes.

## Build and check

Write the sibling:

```bash
node_modules/.bin/dd build path/to/document.dd.json
```

Check without writing:

```bash
node_modules/.bin/dd build path/to/document.dd.json --check
```

The renderer is a pure projection over the parsed document, resolved schema,
preloaded adapters, and precomputed cross-file summaries. It does not read the
filesystem, clock, or process environment. Equal inputs produce equal bytes.

If the existing sibling differs, `--check` returns error `E422` with
`drift: true`. Rebuilding restores the canonical bytes.

## Document heading and metadata

The first object-valued section containing a non-empty `value.title` becomes
the document's `#` heading. If no section carries one, the source filename is
used.

The next line always records:

```text
Schema · source basename · section count
```

Only the basename is rendered. Absolute checkout paths never enter the
markdown.

## Section headings and stable anchors

Every section emits an explicit anchor immediately above its heading:

```markdown
<a id="non-goals"></a>

## Non-goals
```

The anchor is derived from the section `name`. The heading text uses:

1. document section `title`;
2. schema section `title`;
3. title derived from `name`.

This distinction makes a title editable without breaking inbound links. These
all retain `#non-goals`:

```text
Non goals
Non-goals
What we are deliberately not doing
```

The references ledger, when non-empty, renders as a final `References` section
with an unconditional `#references` anchor.

## How section values render

| JSON shape | Markdown form |
| --- | --- |
| object | `Field` / `Value` table |
| array of objects | one table row per object |
| array of scalars | bullet list |
| dynamic-key object map | one `### <key>` subsection per key |
| scalar | block text |
| empty array | `_No entries._` |
| empty object | `_No fields._` |
| blank scalar | `_Empty._` in block context, `—` in a cell |

Declared object fields become columns in schema order. Fields present in data
but absent from the shape follow in first-seen order. Rendering them does not
make them schema-valid; validation remains authoritative.

Nested arrays and objects inside table cells render to a bounded depth. Beyond
two container levels, the cell collapses to `⟨…⟩`; the full value remains in
the JSON.

## Cell safety

Table cells:

- escape `<` and `>`;
- escape `|` so a value cannot split a row;
- convert line breaks to `<br>`;
- use `—` for missing, null, or empty-string values.

This keeps user data inside its cell instead of allowing it to reshape the
generated table.

## States and progress marks

State words remain visible and receive a prefix:

| Mark | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `[x]` | state passes the schema's gate |
| `[ ]` | state holds the gate |
| `[-]` | built-in `blocked` state |
| `[~]` | a derived summary is partially complete |

Examples:

```text
[x] checked
[x] approved
[x] waived
[ ] unchecked
[ ] rejected
[-] blocked
[~] 3/5
```

The word cannot be dropped because custom schemas can declare distinct passing
states.

A link to a state-bearing section can receive a derived summary:

```text
[x] 3/3 [tk-0201](#tk-0201)
```

The summary is computed from the addressed section. It does not reconcile a
separate explicit state field on the row; FU-5 documents that the two can
disagree. See
[Completion states and gates](04-completion-states-and-gates.md#derived-summaries-do-not-reconcile-explicit-state-fields).

## Links

A link to another `.dd.json` renders against its `.dd.md` sibling:

```text
../plan.dd.json#phases/ph-0005
```

becomes:

```markdown
[ph-0005](../plan.dd.md#phases)
```

The visible link text is the last address segment. Array instances land on
their section anchor. Dynamic-key map entries receive their own `###` heading,
so same-document links such as `#done_when/tk-0201` land on `#tk-0201`.

Arrays of declared links render each element as a clickable link.

## Custom types and degraded renders

Custom-type adapters return markdown fragments for their cells. If an adapter
is missing, cannot load, throws, or returns a non-string, the cell renders the
raw value plus a type tag:

```text
`[3,2,1]` ⟨type:sparkline⟩
```

The build writes the rest of the document and returns `degraded` with a warning.
See [Custom types and adapters](06-custom-types-and-adapters.md).

## Fresh cross-file summaries

When a document carries a `live` basis entry for a linked target, rendering
reads the current target and computes the summary from its current section
state. The JSON ledger SHA is not rewritten by build; moved bases are reported
in the build envelope.

See [Freshness and the basis ledger](07-freshness-and-the-basis-ledger.md).
